intended_object: The canonical R-linear isomorphism between the cotangent ideal I/I² ⊆ Sym_R(M)/I² (I the augmentation ideal) and the kernel ideal 0 ⊕ M of the projection R ⊕ M → R in the trivial square-zero extension. It is obtained by restricting the isomorphism Sym_R(M)/I² ≅ R ⊕ M. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `augmentationCotangentEquiv`.
explanation: The body restricts the algebra isomorphism `squareZeroQuotientEquiv : Sym(M)/I² ≃ₐ[R] TrivSqZeroExt R M` to two R-submodules using `LinearEquiv.ofSubmodules`. These are the cotangent ideal I/I² and `TrivSqZeroExt.kerIdeal R M`. The underlying isomorphism is built genuinely, with inverse algebra maps in both directions; it sends the class of ι(m) to inr m and scalars to inl r. The theorem `squareZeroQuotientEquiv_cotangentIdeal` shows the isomorphism maps one ideal exactly onto the other. The result is therefore the canonical isomorphism I/I² ≅ 0 ⊕ M, with the class of ι(m) going to (0, m), as the accompanying simp lemmas confirm. The setting is fully general: any commutative ring R and any R-module M. Mathlib has no ready-made counterpart for this comparison. The definition can also be seen as an intermediate step toward `augmentationCotangentEquiv`, but it is a genuine canonical isomorphism and is correctly formalized.
